answer: In a collateralized network, an attacker launching n Sybil nodes faces capital expenditure growing super-linearly as c n^p plus quadratic slashing bonds s n^2, while extractable value is capped at V. Setting p > 1 and s n^2 + c n^p > V ensures marginal attack cost exceeds gains; this falcon constraint lets the system harbor a fable of bounded loss and positive expected security.
